newsitem.title: MOROCCO: IMF urges Morocco to implement reforms urgently.
newsitem.headline: IMF urges Morocco to implement reforms urgently.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Friday urged Morocco urgently to set up a short-term action plan to implement economic, financial and social reforms to build confidence and attract foreign investors.

Edouard Maciejewski, IMF assistant director for the Middle Eastern Department, told a Euromoney forum attended by nearly 400 delegates from 18 countries: "The time of public aid is over. To get private investment, Morocco should set up a short-term action plan quickly."
He said Morocco "recently succeeded in consolidating its macro-economic fundamentals and returned to a tight control of budget deficit and inflation."
Morocco reduced its budget deficit by 13.5 percent to 23.2 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with the previous year. It also brought inflation to 3.0 percent from 6.1 percent in 1995.
"The country's economy, which is not diversified, remains under threats of weather changes and the impact of agriculture output fluctuations," Maciejewski said.
Agriculture represents an average 20 percent of total GDP which rose to $34.7 billion in 1996 from $31.8 billion in 1995, according to the finance ministry.

The IMF official, who held meetings with Moroccan officials in Rabat, said :"What I noted here is the highest authority will go ahead with reforms and anchor Morocco's economy to the world globalisation...It is a clear message that Morocco wants to be part of the emerging economies."
But there was much to do rapidly, he said, listing the following:
1- Accelerate the privatisation programme of some 70 state-owned companies.
2- Improve administration procedures and investment rules to help foreign investors avoid the existing heavy bureaucracy.
3- Speed up concession procedures in order to involve private sector in local business.
4- Continue the reform of insurance and pension funds.
5- Implement the new investment code and limited company law.
6- Modernise education and combat illiteracy in rural areas to enable future generations to improve their qualifications.
7- Reduce the debt service which stands at 30 percent of Morocco's exports.
8- Build a strong local industry, diversify the country's economy and invest in vital infrastrucures such as roads and telecommunications.

The Public Works Ministry said earlier that annual infrastructure investments were expected to reach $2.3 billion, of which $800 million should come from the private sector mainly from foreign investors.
